svg.title: The adoption rule
svg.desc: compare(usecase, base, candidate) asks six questions in order and the first yes decides. 1: the candidate misses a gate, reject. 2: it has more critical violations than the base, reject. 3: the base misses a gate, adopt. 4: the success interval lies entirely below minus margin, or a guardrail's interval lies entirely past its limit, reject. 5: the success interval lies entirely above 0 and every guardrail stays within its limit, adopt. 6: its success interval has nonzero width, its lower bound is at least minus margin, the cost interval lies below 0 and every guardrail holds, adopt. Steps 4 to 6 require at least six tasks. Otherwise inconclusive: keep the base and add tasks or runs. Equal observed task success rates cannot establish the allowed loss. A number line shows four example intervals and the refund-desk case, where the interval proves nothing but step 3 adopts the workflow because the agent misses the violations gate.
svg.text: The first yes decides. Steps 4–6 require at least six tasks.
Does the candidate miss a gate?
gates are absolute bars, e.g. violations ≤ 0
an average never hides a violation
Does the base miss a gate?
the candidate cleared every gate above
success below −margin, or a guardrail broken
and every guardrail stays within its limit
nonzero success width; cost < 0; guardrails hold
keep the base; add tasks or runs
candidate − base, paired by task, 95% bootstrap
